summary: Discusses the idea of precedence and pre-emption, where more important traffic gets priority when a network is overloaded. It reviews how circuit-switched and message-switched systems do this and considers it for packet networks.

eli5.summary: When a road is jammed, an ambulance gets to go first. This memo asks how a busy network could let urgent messages jump the line.

questions: what is precedence in packet switching
how can tcp pre-empt a connection
subtitle: How high-priority traffic could push aside lower-priority users when a network or a host is saturated.

tldr.problem: When a system runs out of capacity, someone has to decide whose traffic gets through. Circuit and message systems already let high-precedence users win, but packet networks had no stated approach.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC compares how circuit, message and packet systems use precedence, then proposes that processes using TCP keep an extra LISTEN pending so a high-precedence connection request can pre-empt a lower-precedence one.
tldr.outcome: It is a short discussion memo, not a protocol: it needs no new TCP mechanism except making the precedence of incoming connection requests visible to the processes that use TCP.

today: RFC 794 is an Informational memo from September 1981 and the metadata shows no RFC obsoleting or updating it. It describes a strategy for discussion rather than a protocol.

sections.title: Precedence in Three Kinds of Network
sections.content:
In circuit-switching systems, a user who has a circuit keeps its bandwidth even when it is unused, and extra set-up requests are blocked when the system saturates. Systems such as AUTOVON give each telephone instrument a precedence, so a high-precedence instrument can pre-empt circuits and cut off lower-precedence users.

In message-switching systems such as AUTODIN I, messages are stored on disks, drums or tape and processed in order of precedence. A high-precedence message is forwarded as fast as possible and may interrupt the printing of a lower-precedence message at the destination.
sections.eli5: On a phone network the boss's call can bump yours off the line. In a mail room the urgent letter is sorted first.

sections.title: Precedence in Packet Switching
sections.content:
Packet-switching systems have little or no storage, so precedence does little to change the delay for processing a packet. When such a system reaches saturation it rejects offered traffic, and precedence can be used to sort the traffic queued for entry into the system.

The RFC sums it up: precedence is a tool for deciding how to allocate resources when systems are saturated. The resource is circuits in circuit-switched systems, the message switch processor in message-switched systems, and the packet switching system itself in packet switching.
sections.eli5: When there is not enough room for everyone, precedence decides who gets in first.

sections.title: Pre-emption with an Extra LISTEN
sections.content:
The RFC says this can be done in AUTODIN II without adding new mechanisms to TCP, apart from making the precedence of incoming connection requests visible to the processes that use TCP. The software that supports terminal access, called THP, can keep a LISTEN posted for a terminal even while the terminal has a connection in use. If a higher-precedence connection arrives, THP can decide whether to pre-empt the existing one and switch the user to it.

With several connections of different precedence, THP would close or abort the lowest-precedence one in favor of the pre-empting one, then post a new LISTEN. The RFC prefers letting the process that interfaces the terminal decide, because TCP cannot create processes on behalf of an incoming request, and there is no point in creating one if the terminal is off.

Its example: a routine FTP is running between Host X and Host Y, and Host Z opens a flash-override FTP to Host X. FTP always leaves one LISTEN pending when it cannot serve one more user, so it is ready to serve the high-precedence request and clean up after the pre-emption. A non-pre-emptable process is one with no LISTEN pending while it serves users.
sections.eli5: A shopkeeper who always keeps one chair free at the counter can quickly serve an emergency customer. The extra LISTEN is that free chair.

sections.title: Pre-emption at the Source
sections.content:
Pre-emption may also be needed where a high-precedence request starts. If all FTP or TCP resources on the source host are saturated when a high-precedence user tries to start an FTP process, the operating system must know the user's precedence and pre-empt resources locally, for example by logging out lower-precedence users.

The RFC calls this a system issue, not one specific to TCP. Precedence may be tied to a user or to a terminal, the TCP implementation may pre-empt resources locally, or the operating system may make all the decisions.
sections.eli5: If the cafeteria is full, a very important guest may need someone to give up a seat before they can even sit down.
